slides.title: Concepts Overview
slides.prompt: C++20 Concepts specify compile-time constraints on template arguments, replacing complex SFINAE. Declared using `concept` and evaluated with `requires` clauses.

slides.title: Concept Declaration Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used to define a concept in C++20.

slides.title: Requires Clause Placement
slides.prompt: Which of the following syntaxes uses a valid C++20 'requires' clause?
options: template <typename T> requires std::integral<T> void print(T val);
template <typename T constraint std::integral> void print(T val);
template <typename T> where std::integral<T> void print(T val);
template <typename T if std::integral<T>> void print(T val);
slides.correctAnswer: template <typename T> requires std::integral<T> void print(T val);

slides.title: Abbreviated Function Template Syntax
slides.prompt: C++20 allows constrained auto function parameters. Fill in the constrained auto syntax.

slides.title: Requires Expression compound constraint
slides.prompt: What does '{ expr } -> std::same_as<int>;' enforce inside a C++20 requires expression?
options: The expression 'expr' must be valid AND its return type must satisfy std::same_as<int>
It casts the result of 'expr' to int automatically
It executes 'expr' at runtime and checks return equality
It declares a lambda function returning int
slides.correctAnswer: The expression 'expr' must be valid AND its return type must satisfy std::same_as<int>

slides.title: Concepts Header
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard C++20 header file required for standard library concepts like std::integral.

slides.title: Concept Overload Subsumption
slides.prompt: How does C++20 handle template overloads when multiple concepts match the provided argument?
options: Selects the function constrained by the MORE SPECIFIC concept (subsumption rule)
Throws a compile-time ambiguity error in all cases
Selects the first declared overload in source code order
Falls back to non-constrained generic template
slides.correctAnswer: Selects the function constrained by the MORE SPECIFIC concept (subsumption rule)

slides.title: Combining Constraints Operator
slides.prompt: Fill in the logical operator used to combine concepts in a requires clause.

slides.title: Concept Evaluation Context
slides.prompt: When are C++20 Concepts evaluated by the compiler?
options: At compile time during template specialization/instantiation candidate filtering
At application startup prior to main()
At runtime when entering the function body
slides.correctAnswer: At compile time during template specialization/instantiation candidate filtering

slides.title: Requires Clause Keyword
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword used both to start constraint clauses and open nested constraint blocks.
